note: Cristallo liquido ionico 1-Bf (sale di imidazolio con BF4–, nucleo azobenzenico): due polimorfi di partenza (α-Cr, forma lineare L; β-Cr, forma 'step-stair' SS), una fase cristallina intermedia i-Cr (supercooled, con regioni amorfe, solo SAXS/XRD) e il cold crystal cc-Cr, che gli autori identificano con β-Cr («we identified the β-Cr phase as the cc-Cr»): una sola forma F2 con due strutture (β-Cr e cc-Cr, CCDC 2024816 e 2024817, entrambe a 93.15 K; cella di cc-Cr in nota). Le fasi liquido-cristalline sono estratte come forme: SmA (smectica A, tipo altro) e Iso (liquido isotropo, tipo fuso, usato come 'da' nelle trasformazioni di raffreddamento; la fusione verso il liquido isotropo e' scritta a: fuso). Tutte le temperature di transizione sono onset («The onset temperature of thermal anomaly is defined as the phase transition temperature throughout this work») e le rampe sono ±5.0 °C/min (+ in riscaldamento, − in raffreddamento). La transizione vetrosa vista in riscaldamento prima della cristallizzazione fredda («the endothermic peak anomaly observed immediately before the exothermic anomaly upon heating around Tcc is identified as a glass transition partially coupled to the cold crystallization») e' dentro l'i-Cr, non e' un evento di forma; non si osserva Tg in raffreddamento. Il comportamento termico oltre il terzo ciclo e' detto simile al secondo («The thermal behavior of the crystal beyond the third thermal cycle was similar to the second cycle»): nessun evento nuovo. Incoerenza dell'articolo: punto di fusione di α-Cr 123.6 °C (Tm1–1, Risultati, Figura 3) contro 122.5 °C (parte sperimentale, «with a melting point of 122.5 °C (first heating process)»), entrambi onset del primo riscaldamento. Anche la frase «that transformed the cc-Cr to SmA» sull'inizio del secondo ciclo e' formulata male (la cold crystallization e' i-Cr → cc-Cr).

citazioni: DSC analysis of the initial crystal revealed that 1-Bf underwent a series of phase transitions (Figure 3). They are, namely, from the initial crystal phase (α-Cr) to the liquid crystal phase (SmA) (Tm1–1: 123.6 °C) and melting from SmA to an isotropic liquid phase (Iso) (Tm1–2: 155.1 °C) during the first heating process.
The phase transition behavior of 1-Bf was investigated between −30 and 180 °C using a differential scanning calorimeter (Mettler Toledo, DSC-1).

Measurements were conducted under a N2 atmosphere (50 mL min–1) using an aluminum open pan at a scanning rate of ±5.0 °C min–1. The onset temperature of thermal anomaly is defined as the phase transition temperature throughout this work.

Upon first heating at approximately Tm1–1, at which point the α-Cr transitions into SmA, the FTIR spectra above Tm1–1 closely matched that of in β-Cr, suggesting that a conformational alteration occurred, which changed the L-form in α-Cr to the SS-form in β-Cr.

In summary, the cold crystal of 1-Bf consists of cations in the step-stair conformation that is irreversibly formed after the first melting of the initial crystal, α-Cr, at Tm1–1. This molecular conformation persists throughout the subsequent phases: Iso, SmA, i-Cr, and cc-Cr.
eventi.note: Primo riscaldamento di α-Cr (Sample-I): fusione a cristallo liquido SmA a Tm1–1 = 123.6 °C (onset). Nella parte sperimentale: «orange needle-shaped crystals (α-Cr) with a melting point of 122.5 °C (first heating process)» (stesso onset del primo riscaldamento, valore diverso): scelto 123.6 (Risultati con Figura 3). Alla transizione i cationi passano irreversibilmente dalla forma lineare (L) a quella step-stair (SS) (FTIR sopra Tm1–1 simile a β-Cr).

citazioni: Upon cooling, a phase transition from Iso to SmA (Tc1–1: 155.0 °C) and crystallization from SmA (Tc1–2: 37.6 °C) to an intermediate supercooled crystalline phase i-Cr, the details of which will be given later, were observed.

Interestingly, continued cooling below Tc1–2 induced a transition from SmA to i-Cr, leading to the emergence of a diffraction pattern, namely, the broadened SAXS peaks at 2θ = 3.0–3.3 and 6.0–6.6 °, suggestive of c-axis contraction to varying degrees (Figure 4A-iii), distinct from that of the initial crystal (α-Cr).

Specifically, nuclei were formed from SmA and subsequently grew into i-Cr by aggregating into microcrystals that served as the seed crystal for the growth of the β-Cr. In other words, the i-Cr acted as an intermediate crystal phase for the formation of the cc-Cr (β-Cr).

Upon further cooling from SmA to i-Cr and finally to β-Cr, the two peaks (857 and 840 cm–1) did not show a significant change, indicating that the SS-form was maintained throughout the crystalline phases.

citazioni: The second heating cycle involved recrystallization (i.e., cold crystallization, Tcc: 42.2 °C) that transformed the cc-Cr to SmA (Tm2–1: 115.9 °C) and finally to Iso (Tm2–2: 154.9 °C).

Further heating of cc-Cr (β-Cr) resulted in a transition to SmA stabilized between Tm2–1 (115.9 °C) and Tm2–2 (154.9 °C), which was accompanied by a shift in the 001 and 002 reflections in the cc-Cr (β-Cr) (Figure 5A-vii) and the disappearance of higher angle diffraction peaks (Figure 5B-xi). Finally, above Tm2–2, no diffraction peaks were observed in the entire 2θ range, indicating a transition into the Iso (Figure 5A-viii,B-xii).

The cold crystal in the second heating cycle exhibited a melting point (Tm2–1) 7.7 °C lower than that of the initial crystal (Tm1–1), indicating that the cold crystal was thermodynamically less stable than the initial crystal (Figure 3 and Table S1).

citazioni: By conducting thorough structural characterization, we found that the prerequisite for cold crystallization is the irreversible molecular conformational alteration induced by the initial heating of the as-grown crystal into a smectic liquid crystal. The originally linear cation molecule bends and forms a step-stair conformation that persists throughout the subsequent heating and cooling processes as phase transition occurs from the crystal phase to the liquid crystal phase and then to the isotropic liquid phase.

In summary, the cold crystal of 1-Bf consists of cations in the step-stair conformation that is irreversibly formed after the first melting of the initial crystal, α-Cr, at Tm1–1. This molecular conformation persists throughout the subsequent phases: Iso, SmA, i-Cr, and cc-Cr.

Interestingly, continued cooling below Tc1–2 induced a transition from SmA to i-Cr, leading to the emergence of a diffraction pattern, namely, the broadened SAXS peaks at 2θ = 3.0–3.3 and 6.0–6.6 °, suggestive of c-axis contraction to varying degrees (Figure 4A-iii), distinct from that of the initial crystal (α-Cr).

Measurements were conducted under a N2 atmosphere (50 mL min–1) using an aluminum open pan at a scanning rate of ±5.0 °C min–1. The onset temperature of thermal anomaly is defined as the phase transition temperature throughout this work.

Nessuna temperatura propria: il raffreddamento va da SmA (Tc1–2 = 37.6 °C per la cristallizzazione, E4).

citazioni: The crude product was dissolved in dichloromethane, recrystallized, and dried under vacuum for 24 h to obtain pure orange needle-shaped crystals of 1-Bf (1.3 g, 65%), which we define as the α phase (α-Cr).

citazioni: A half portion of the initial crystals was further dissolved in ethanol and recrystallized (0.5 g, 79%), which we define as the β phase (β-Cr).

citazioni: Similarly, crystal fragments (0.02 × 0.02 × 0.01 mm3) of Sample-II after DSC analysis and cooled to room temperature (Sample-III) are defined as a cold crystal (cc-Cr).
preparazioni.note: Il cold crystal per SCXRD (Sample-III) sono frammenti di Sample-II dopo il DSC e raffreddati a temperatura ambiente; il ciclo termico esatto di questo campione non e' descritto, il legame con E5 (cristallizzazione fredda di i-Cr descritta per Sample-I) segue l'identificazione β-Cr = cc-Cr.

proprieta.metodo: calcolo ONIOM (differenza di energia fra le conformazioni L e SS)
proprieta.citazione: Combined with the negligible energy difference (∼1 kJ mol–1) between the two conformations obtained from the calculations, these results suggest that the intermolecular Coulombic interaction plays a crucial role in the series of crystallization processes (Table S4).

grandezza.testo: endothermic anomaly immediately before the cold crystallization exotherm (around Tcc), partially coupled to it; no Tg observed on cooling

proprieta.metodo: DSC dipendente dalla velocita' di scansione (Figura S4)
proprieta.citazione: We note that a glass transition (Tg) was not observed in the cooling process, and the endothermic peak anomaly observed immediately before the exothermic anomaly upon heating around Tcc is identified as a glass transition partially coupled to the cold crystallization, based on a series of sweep rate dependent thermal analysis (Figure S4).

descrizioni.testo: irreversible change from the linear to the step-stair conformation at the first melting of the initial crystal; the cold crystallization selects the SS-form, more metastable than the linear form
descrizioni.citazione: Overall, the cold crystallization of 1-Bf is a crystallization process that selects the step-stair conformation that is more metastable than the linear form in the initial crystal.
